I live in Texas and I can not seem to get the temp in our house to go below 76 degrees from 5 to 8 PM. Our home is energy efficient, it was built in 2012, it has dual pained windows, high ceilings, fans in all the rooms, we keep all the doors for the rooms open to allow air to circulate, each room has an intake and a duct that blows cold air out. We keep the exterior doors closed as much as possible, we do not have a dog door or anything like that to let the cold out. Any ideas would be appreciated.
Request a discussion on how to help keep your home cool during the summer!

Do you have one of those usage boxes on your central air unit that lets the power company turn it off and on? In my area they have a terrible habit of turning them off during the hottest parts of the day. Most people I know bypass them completely or let the house get extremely cold while they're at work so it's not a sweatbox when they get home.

I am not aware of a box on the unit itself that allows them to do that, if I found it, I would not be happy at all. My wife is home all day, and she says the A/C is staying on all day. The issue also seems to be getting worse... Last night the A/C ran for most all of the night. The second story is getting colder than the first story so I think there is an issue the the down stairs A/C.
We are also considering solar screens because the sun hits the back of the house pretty hard between the same times.

I used to live in Cyprus - 40 degrees Celsius in summer - is there any way of shading your home on the sunniest side by planting a tree or shrubs? Indoor water features and house plants can also make the house feel cooler. You should also keep blinds or shades closed on windows to keep the sun out- even if it just a light voile curtain. Makes such a difference to your house heating up.
Trees always help, if they are large enough.

I agree with this one in a big way, I am saving now to get two full size apple trees for next year. I plan to put them right in the path of the sun during the evening time, I am sure fruit trees will not be the absolute best for shade, but I am sure they will help some and give us some free food.
I don't know how citrus works in your part of the world, but orange trees can be really dense, so can avocados.

I think one of the main things is a large attic fan. Pulls the hot air out of the attic when it cools for the night, and if designed correctly, also draws cool air into the house. Cost is about $1,000 installed, if I remember correctly.

Update

I had the AC unit tested for leaks, and sure enough the first floor unit has a leak in it. It was out of Freon, the guy recharged the unit and it is working just fine now. The unit itself is still under warranty so it is a down hill process from here.

I am still going to keep an eye on this thread and still plan on putting two full size trees in the back left corner of the house to help shade it from the 5 o'clock sun
